A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plan-of-SQLs work. Their text, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across reformatting, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original Table QA experiments, human and LLM explanation evaluations, and appendix analyses of planning and SQL execution.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds human–LLM agreement measurements, additional LLM judges, component ablations, table-size analysis and self-explanation comparisons.

M1.justification: Atomic natural-language planning, Step-to-SQL, sequential execution and attribution tracking are retained. The FeTaQA adaptation and one-step planner already appear in v1. Section 5's SQL validation/regeneration pipeline is presented as a proposed enhancement, without establishing a change to the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use TabFact verification, WikiTQ question answering and FeTaQA free-form answering, and retain the same human study. V2's table-size bins partition existing test data; additional judge models change experimental configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds a post-hoc self-explanation baseline to preference, forward-simulation and verification comparisons on TabFact (Appendix B, Table 10). The existing Text-to-SQL, DATER and CoTable explanation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o-mini benchmark comparisons, Qwen2.5-72B and Llama-3.1-405B judges, agreement measurements on matched human-response subsets, five-method preference ranking, and equal-sized token-count bins. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original dataset splits and 32-person, 800-response human study remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's qualitative atomicity examples, planning errors and SQL-versus-LLM analysis, v2 adds quantitative verification ablations of atomicity, natural-language planning and SQL execution (Table 5), table-size sensitivity analysis (Table 7), and judge-family and human–LLM agreement analyses. The appendix one-step planning experiment is retained.

E5.justification: Both retain preference averaging over four presentation orders and the original Pearson correlations with p-values. The new table-size correlations reuse Pearson estimation; no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o-mini QA scores, including POS's 82.70% on TabFact and 59.32% on WikiTQ, plus new explanation, agreement, ablation and size results. Original GPT-3.5, FeTaQA and one-step planning scores remain unchanged. V1 Appendix K's WikiTQ drop from 48.90% to 27.05% is omitted, and its slight TabFact increase becomes a decrease in Section 4.2.3. New Table 7 contains inconsistent percentages and counts.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and atomicity constraints are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are added; the stronger faithfulness assertions remain prose claims.

C1.justification: The interpretability, competitive accuracy, efficiency and LLM-proxy claims remain. V2 adds comparative robustness on large tables to its central contributions and strengthens the introduction's priority claim from 'among the first' to 'the first.'

C2.justification: V2 interprets SQL execution and planning as more important than atomicity for interpretability, and adds discussion of noisy tables, fallback handling and opaque LLM internals. It also asserts absolute faithfulness/comprehensiveness and extrapolates robustness to million-token tables. The FeTaQA comparison is explicitly qualified as demonstrating adaptability rather than optimized accuracy.

D1.justification: V2 supplies repository and interactive-interface links, additional model/provider identifiers, and a self-explanation prompt. Conversely, Appendix A removes the explicit GPT-3.5 model identifier previously given for explanation generation. Most detailed prompts and SQL attribution implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on self-explanation faithfulness, automated simulatability and concept bottlenecks, and replaces the SQLite background reference. It more explicitly contrasts POS with TaPERA's subjective faithfulness/comprehensiveness evaluation, while retaining the overall related-work framework.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution list, related-work passages and Appendix A, and reorganizes the experimental narrative. Baseline descriptions move from Appendix B into the main text, FeTaQA moves after efficiency, and a Discussion section is added. 'Debugging' becomes 'verification' without changing the task.

P2.justification: V2 adds five result tables and a self-explanation figure, and expands the main accuracy table with GPT-4o-mini results. The publication template changes author layout, typography, captions and prompt boxes throughout; retained figures and appendix examples are resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: Matched human–LLM agreement, additional judge families, component ablations and the self-explanation baseline provide better targeted evidence for the central interpretability claims than v1. These benefits are tempered by Table 7's arithmetic inconsistencies—for example, 713/1448 is 49.2%, not 56.1%—unsupported extrapolation to million-token tables, and removal of exact SQL-ablation results.
